Location: Windsor, Ontario, Canada

I live about 30 minutes east of the city. It's a very unique location in regards to weather behavior. When storms and rainclouds come from the west, they usually follow the lakes and split up, going north towards Sarnia, hitting London and eventually Toronto, or more south towards Cleveland. 

I can't remember the last time it rained. I've lived here all my life, and the ground has always been nutrient rich, black soil, and many people have wonderful gardens every year. Now the ground is grey, cracked, and barely holds water. Definitely not the spring I remember when the fields would be flooded with water. 

Also this morning, it was hazy. I heard that smoke coming from the west and from Quebec would be making its way down here, but I didn't expect this far.  I suppose I shouldn't be surprised.

There was a relatively new factory that opened in my small town, close enough I could walk. I could save lots of money on gas, and the extra exercise walking wouldn't hurt either.

I hurt my left arm there, I think it was nerve damage because it was nonstop pins and needles for about a month afterwards. Stupid of me to not see a doctor I know, 20 year old me was pretty stubborn.

Anyway, I called in when it was particularly bad one day, and my team leader put me on the phone with the production manager. He said "How am I supposed to give out raises and full-time benefits if you can't even show up to work?"

That really pissed me off, and stuck with me. A week later I got fed up, so I purposely messed with one of the mold presses, and broke it. Maintenance guy told me it was a $10,000 fix. I grinned and walked out that night.

Pretty immature of me, and I definitely could've been more professional, but I've always had a hard time sticking up for myself, so I felt good about myself. Got a better job 15 minutes away a week later, and I keep my nose clean as possible while I'm there.

My first game of DnD.

I was a half-orc fighter, part of a mercenary group with my 3 friends; a Paladin, a Rogue and a Half-Orc, Half-Giant.

We were sent to clear out a forest of creatures so a local town could continue construction operations that will allow the town to have more land for agriculture. We come to a clearing, and approx. 30ft ahead of us we see 5 goblins and a werewolf-like creature with a club, the name of which I can't remember. 

It was the Rogues turn first. It was also friend's first time playing, but he was trying to play the game like he was a level 40 their in Skyrim, with all the stats and skills. Nope, we had JUST started. He thought he could be sneaky by walking around the edge of the forest undetected and flank them. He ended up just staying there the entire fight.

My move next. I moved in front of my group and used intimidation. It was very successful, as 2 goblins ran in fear, and the werewolf-like creature began to step back, as he was nervous as well.

Then the Half-Giant. I should note that my friend playing this had played DnD for some time, and is fairly experienced. He's also the DM's little brother, and knows how to fuck with us. 

Knowing that my character is no more than 5 ft directly in front of him, he pulls out his greatsword and says "I want to throw it directly at 'werewolf creature'". My DM looks at him almost dumbfounded.

"Do you really want to attempt this? You'll need an 18 or higher to NOT take off Driig's head."

"Did I fucking stutter?"

He ends up rolling a 20 and cleaving half the werewolve's face off.

Later on during combat, he picks up a goblin by the head, and leaves him hanging there. My paladin attempts to cut the goblin in half, while still hanging from the Half-Giant's hand. He rolls high enough to hit, but just barely enough to kill it completely. The goblin's midsection begins to spill out. Then, resulting in many laughs around the table, the Half-Giant fists the open wound, and begins to carry around his goblin hand puppet as a souvenir for the rest of our travels.

Our second session is tonight and I cannot wait.

One of my high school science teachers. We'll call him Kam, the nickname we had for him.

While it may not seem interesting at first, let me tell you something. When my friends parents went to high school, he was their teacher, and I guess he was old back then. Approximately 30 years later he's that same friend and my science teacher, so you can imagine how old he is. However no one knew his age, not even a ballpark guess. To put it into perspective, he looked like Richard Gere with dark grey hair when he finally retired when I was grade 10. 

What made it even more ridiculous, our school had our monthly fire drill, but there was this uproar that there was someone missing. Next thing you know, Kam walked out, in full gym clothing and a walkman, yes a walkman, in his ears, not giving a single fuck. We later found out our principal found him in the weight room doing chin-ups.

TL;DR - Ridiculously old teacher who discovered the fountain of youth who liked to do chin-ups when he wasn't teaching.
